name: Plum Pudding, Without Eggs
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: finely-chopped beef suet
ingredients.originalText: one cupful of finely-chopped beef suet

ingredients.name: fine bread crumbs
ingredients.originalText: two cupfuls of fine bread crumbs

ingredients.name: carbonate of soda
ingredients.originalText: one teaspoonful of carbonate of soda

instructions.text: Stir thoroughly together the finely-chopped beef suet, fine bread crumbs, molasses, chopped raisins, well-washed currants, salt, cloves, cinnamon, allspice and carbonate of soda
Add one cupful of milk and flour enough to make a stiff batter
Put into a well-greased pudding-mold, or a three-quart pail and cover closely
Set this pail into a larger kettle, close covered, and half full of boiling water, adding boiling water as it boils away
Steam not less than four hours
Serve with wine sauce or common sweet sauce

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Stir thoroughly together the finely-chopped beef suet, fine bread crumbs, molasses, chopped raisins, well-washed currants, salt, cloves, cinnamon, allspice and carbonate of soda
2. Add one cupful of milk and flour enough to make a stiff batter
3. Put into a well-greased pudding-mold, or a three-quart pail and cover closely
4. Set this pail into a larger kettle, close covered, and half full of boiling water, adding boiling water as it boils away
5. Steam not less than four hours
6. Serve with wine sauce or common sweet sauce

two cupfuls of fine bread crumbs
one teaspoonful of carbonate of soda
